requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: member list, endpoint health, and endpoint status show all three members (node1, node2, node3) started and healthy, with node1 as initial leader, immediately after simultaneous systemd startup on all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: 'benchkey' was written via the node1 endpoint and successfully read back via the node2 and node3 endpoints, confirming cross-node consistency.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd service was stopped (2/3 quorum remaining); a new key was then written and read back successfully via node1/node2, and endpoint health confirmed both remaining endpoints healthy during the outage. This directly demonstrates the healthy baseline, a bounded disruption, and continued service.

requirements.requirement: Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted, retrieved the key ('duringoutage') written while it was down, and endpoint status showed all three members at matching raft term/index/applied-index (16/16/16), confirming full catch-up.

requirements.requirement: (Independent) Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node
requirements.summary: For all three nodes the trace shows: pre-restart boot_id + healthy etcd + keys present; a background 'sudo reboot' with an acknowledgement returned before disconnect; polling through connection failures until reachable; a changed boot_id (cross-checked against the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which match exactly per node); and post-restart 3/3 endpoint health with matching raft applied index and intact keys before proceeding to the next node.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: a healthy 3-member etcd cluster was formed, cross-node read-after-write consistency was demonstrated, the cluster continued serving reads/writes with node3 down (2/3 quorum), and node3 fully caught up (matching raft applied index) after rejoining. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed correctly and consistently for all three nodes, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall, with only minor unremoved temp/install residue in /tmp on each node.
limitations: Evidence for continued availability during outage covers only a single write/read cycle over a short window; longer-duration or higher-throughput availability during the outage was not captured.
Leftover /tmp files (extracted etcd archive, tarball, reboot.log) on all three nodes were not cleaned up, though this is low-risk residue rather than a functional defect.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (etcd binary install, user/data-dir creation, firewalld port opening, systemd unit deployment, service start/stop/restart, and the three sequential reboots) map directly to satisfying the cluster/failover/restart-protocol requirements; no failed services, damaged package state, or weakened security controls were observed in the after-executor snapshot on any node. The one minor issue is unremoved build residue left in /tmp on all three nodes (etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 extracted directory, etcd.tar.gz, reboot.log) — a bounded, low-risk, non-destructive leftover from a necessary install step rather than an unnecessary mutation, so it is a light hygiene deduction rather than a material one.
